name: Testosterone replacement therapy
lead: Testosterone replacement therapy (TRT) is the medical supplementation of testosterone to restore normal levels in people with hypogonadism, mainly men. It can be given by injection, gel, patch, pellet or oral forms.[1][2]

Testosterone can deepen the voice in some people, such as women or transgender men receiving it, as part of virilization.[3] In men with low testosterone, trials have reported increases in fat-free mass and muscle size.[4]
Safety has been debated: a 2004 review recommended monitoring, and the 2023 TRAVERSE trial studied cardiovascular safety. The FDA changed boxed-warning language in 2025.[3][5][6]
infobox: US Schedule III; UK Class C; Rx in EU[3]

paras: The main indication is male hypogonadism confirmed by testing and symptoms; it is also used in transgender men and for some cancers.[1][3] A 2020 American College of Physicians guideline supports discussing it for age-related low levels with sexual dysfunction.[3]

A 1997 study reported that testosterone replacement increased fat-free mass and muscle size in hypogonadal men.[4] Trials in hypogonadal men with type 2 diabetes reported effects on insulin resistance, glycaemic control and adiposity.[7][8]

A 2004 review set out risks and monitoring recommendations.[5] The 2023 TRAVERSE trial found no increase in adverse cardiovascular outcomes in hypogonadal men, and in 2025 the FDA revised the boxed warning and added blood pressure language.[3][6]
Reported effects include acne, hair loss, suppressed sperm production, higher hematocrit and worsened sleep apnea.[3]
In women testosterone can cause voice deepening and other virilizing signs.[3] Evidence on voice in men receiving replacement is not reported in these sources.

Studies include the TRAVERSE cardiovascular safety trial, the TIMES2 diabetes and metabolic syndrome study, and a double-blind crossover trial in men with type 2 diabetes, plus registered trials in kidney transplant, prostate cancer surveillance and hypogonadism.[6][7][8][9][10] No studies were found of TRT for voice deepening.

card.summary: Medical testosterone for low levels; can deepen voice via virilization, studied for muscle and metabolic outcomes in hypogonadal men.
card.note: Requires diagnosis and monitoring; controlled substance in many countries.

quick.overview:
TRT supplements testosterone in people with diagnosed deficiency. In hypogonadal men, trials report gains in muscle and metabolic markers.

Testosterone can deepen the voice in women or transgender men; voice is not a studied TRT goal.
quick.mechanism: Exogenous testosterone restores androgen receptor signaling and suppresses the body's own production through feedback on the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis.
quick.risks: Reported risks include raised hematocrit, sleep apnea, fertility suppression, acne, prostate concerns, and cardiovascular questions addressed by TRAVERSE; FDA warnings were revised in 2025.
